Intro.title: Building the Future of Medical Education
Intro.body: ASCEL provides an environment where doctors can develop practical skills through simulation, experimental learning, education, and collaboration. The center is being established in the city of Gyumri to develop the practical skills of doctors and to support a regional culture of professional medical education.

AboutPage.title: A center for medical education, practical training and professional practice
AboutPage.whoBody: The Gyumri Medical Training Center is being created inside the monument house at 20-22 Myasnikyan Street as a center for practical medical education. The aim is to close gaps in hands-on skills preparation and to serve as a regional hub for medical education.
AboutPage.missionBody: To create a professional environment where doctors and learners can develop practical skills through a cadaver lab, structured teaching space and international collaboration.
AboutPage.visionBody: To help Armenia become a regional center for advanced medical education and practical professional training — serious, international in standard, and grounded in practical competence.
AboutPage.whatBody: The center brings together medical education, practical training and related programs. Active strands include Gyumri Orthopedic School, the Damage Control Courses, and a partnership presentation of Eternal Nation Foundation — each distinct, under one institutional platform.
AboutPage.simulationBody: The center's working level — a 93 m² operating room and a cadaver lab — lets teams rehearse procedures, communication and decision-making in a controlled setting before any of it is needed in clinical care.
AboutPage.experimentalBody: Experimental learning here means structured, practical methods beyond the lecture: skills labs, scenario-based teaching and, within ethical rules, the advanced methods used in international medical education.
AboutPage.developmentBody: The center is conceived as a setting for continuing education — courses, workshops, and collaborative teaching that help physicians and related professionals strengthen practical competence.
AboutPage.collaborationBody: The center is designed to work with faculty and partners from Armenia and abroad. Confirmed institutional partnerships will be listed once cleared for publication.
AboutPage.approachBody: The design of the center is educational first: clear programs, practical teaching and a calm professional environment. Programs stay distinguishable. Independent partner organizations are not presented as the same legal entity.
AboutPage.timelineItem1Body: The center was presented as a healthcare education project working towards a medical training center in Gyumri, including as a featured project at AMWC 2025.

ProjectHero.headline: An abandoned monument in Gyumri becomes a medical training center
ProjectHero.supporting: The 19th-century house at 20-22 Myasnikyan Street has stood for years with its windows bricked up and its roof collapsing. The project restores it and creates 713.92 m² of teaching space inside and beneath it: an operating room, a cadaver lab, study rooms and a library. Construction depends on donations.
ProjectHero.imageAlt: The restored monument facade seen from Myasnikyan Street, under its new wave roof

ProjectIntro.title: One address, one building, one purpose
ProjectIntro.body: This is not an abstract programme. It has an address — 20-22 Myasnikyan Street, Gyumri, parcel 08-001-1333-0029 — and a completed sketch design. The monument is kept whole, and the extra space the brief needs is found in two ways: underground, and in a volume invisible from the street.
ProjectIntro.bodySecond: That keeps the building's height at the scale of the neighbourhood while the dark, technical zones — the operating room and the lab — drop to the basement level. 335.79 m² of the site is planted: an inner courtyard and a roof terrace.
ProjectIntro.imageAlt: The project within Gyumri's urban fabric, seen from the air
ProjectIntro.figuresNote: Figures are taken from the technical indicators table of the sketch design dated 07.11.2026.

CadaverLab.title: Why the center needs a basement
CadaverLab.body: A cadaver medical laboratory is a specialised educational environment where healthcare students and professionals carry out detailed dissections of the human body in order to study anatomy.
CadaverLab.bodySecond: These laboratories are a formative experience: they let students touch and examine tissue, and understand anatomical features that digital models cannot fully convey.
CadaverLab.note: Level −3.900 holds a 93.01 m² operating room, a 34.30 m² vet lab, cold storage and changing rooms — 215.33 m² in total.

CenterPage.title: The Gyumri Medical Training Center project
CenterPage.intro: Restoring the monument house at 20-22 Myasnikyan Street and turning it into a medical training center with an operating room, a cadaver lab, study rooms, a library and a courtyard.
CenterPage.imageAlt: The restored monument facade seen from Myasnikyan Street, under its new wave roof
CenterPage.closing: The design is ready; what is missing is the money to build. Support of any size goes to a specific piece of work — from a single window to the whole roof.
